statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the unauthenticated entry, redirected product page, related product/pricing templates and sign-in journey up to the credential boundary. Authenticated mailbox content and account-management internals were not covered.

page.framework: Microsoft Outlook boot shell redirecting to Microsoft 365 product templates; Microsoft identity sign-in
page.notes: Unauthenticated outlook.live.com attempts silent auth, then redirects to a localized public Microsoft 365 Outlook page. The target therefore spans an app boot/redirect plus a marketing MPA. Not covered: authenticated inbox/calendar, message compose, subscription cancellation after login, other locales beyond en-GB, and native apps.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline summary was 49.5 MB/653,666 nodes; after dismissing consent and exercising tabs ten times it was 59.7 MB/839,165 nodes. The capture includes one-time full-page activation, so it is a risk signal rather than proof of a leak.
The post-interaction heap summary reports 59.7 MB self size, 839,165 nodes and 3,056,272 edges, alongside a 9.0 MB transfer and duplicated app/marketing code.
Neither heap summary reports Detached* constructors among retained top constructors; the Popover constructor remains stable at 167 across captures.

paths.description: Entry URL and redirected Outlook marketing/product page; covers discovery, consent, primary calls to action, security, performance and metadata.
Narrow viewport rendition of the entry journey; covers reflow, overflow and touch-sized layout.
Outlook on the web product-detail archetype discovered from primary navigation.
Consumer plans/pricing archetype discovered from the product page; reviewed for commercial clarity.
Primary sign-in journey up to the credential boundary; reviewed for labels, autofill, recovery and modern-auth affordances.

findings.summary: The public Outlook landing experience does not adapt to a dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-identical in the visible consent and navigation surface; both remain light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint page, consent, navigation and controls with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: State changes use abrupt swaps rather than coherent view transitions.
findings.evidence: The interaction video records a product-tab change and smooth scroll but no transition connecting the old and new tab state; the CSS feature probe found no view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for meaningful tab/panel changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The very long product page offers little position-aware guidance.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 16,783 CSS px tall, while the interaction video and CSS probe show no progress indicator or scroll-state-aware page chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or section-aware navigation treatment that does not obscure content.

findings.summary: Consent and announcement chrome dominate the initial viewport.
findings.evidence: The first desktop screenshot shows the cookie choice taking roughly two thirds of the viewport, followed immediately by navigation and another announcement banner; core Outlook content is not visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent panel footprint, preserve equal Accept/Reject choices, and avoid stacking another banner before primary content.

findings.summary: Overlay-like UI is implemented without semantic dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover and 0 details elements while the initial surface presents cookie controls and dismissible announcement UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for truly modal consent and popover for transient UI, including declarative dismissal and focus management.

findings.summary: Application chrome crowds out the product message on entry.
findings.evidence: The initial desktop viewport contains consent copy, three consent controls, two navigation rows and an announcement bar, with no product heading or primary Outlook action visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse redundant chrome and ensure the product purpose and primary action remain in the first viewport.

findings.summary: The page purpose and primary Outlook action are hidden on initial load.
findings.evidence: The entry screenshot exposes no Outlook heading, sign-in or account-creation action before consent, global navigation and an announcement; the product H1 exists lower in the DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep necessary consent compact and bring the Outlook purpose plus Sign in/Create account actions into the initial visual hierarchy.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is far outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 11.4 s, LCP 24.4 s, TBT 2,970 ms, CLS 0.53, and time to interactive 35.2 s; performance score was 0.05.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the redirect and LCP chain, eliminate nonessential startup work, reserve layout space, and prioritize only the hero-critical resources.

findings.summary: The entry journey transfers an excessive, highly fragmented payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 151 requests and 9,016,578 transferred bytes: 77 scripts (4.03 MB), 27 stylesheets, 1.12 MB fonts and a 1.65 MB media file, plus many parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid loading both app boot and marketing stacks, shorten redirects and critical CSS chains, subset fonts, and defer media and noncritical modules.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JS and CSS ship on the landing journey.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 951 KiB unused JavaScript and 342 KiB unused CSS; individual bundles were 55-73% unused and global CSS files were 81-98% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles, remove duplicate app/marketing utilities, and conditionally load video, feedback and Outlook-app code after user intent.

findings.summary: Some rendered images and the global search input lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 15 images without alt text, and the quality probe found the visible search input had no associated label or ARIA label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images concise alt text, mark decorative images with alt="", and provide a programmatic label for search.

findings.summary: Heading structure is repetitive and skips levels.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found four identical H1 elements; Lighthouse reported invalid heading order where plan-card text jumps to H6. Keyboard focus indicators themselves were visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Render one page H1 per active responsive variant and use semantic heading levels based on document hierarchy rather than visual size.

findings.summary: Duplicate scripts throw repeated syntax errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured repeated SyntaxError exceptions: LocalStorageUtil and OneCloudUtil identifiers were declared more than once.
findings.suggestedFix: Deduplicate the OneCloud/local-storage bundles and add a smoke test that fails on uncaught page-load exceptions.

findings.summary: Image markup does not reserve intrinsic space and some images are oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 100 img elements lacked width/height attributes, three were over 2x their display width, six lacked responsive sources, and one used a legacy format.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and use correctly sized srcset/sizes with modern formats.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handlers block the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported unload listeners in both the Outlook mini-index and Microsoft telemetry code, one actionable BFCache failure, and two deprecation warnings.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange and verify BFCache restoration in DevTools.

findings.summary: Several controls are not crawlable links and many link labels are generic.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found six anchors using javascript:void(0) and 26 links labelled only “Learn more”; the rendered page otherwise has a viewport meta and robots.txt is valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real href URLs for navigation, and destination-specific link text.

findings.summary: The product page lacks structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found five Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks on a public software/product page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate SoftwareApplication/Product and Organization JSON-LD aligned with visible product and plan content.

findings.summary: The entry journey has a very large third-party and telemetry footprint before user intent.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 143 of 151 requests and 8.80 MB to origins other than outlook.live.com; requests include Microsoft telemetry and a third-party video origin. Lighthouse also observed 15 third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat Microsoft-owned cross-origin services as supply-chain dependencies: defer telemetry/media until consent or intent, batch events, and reduce origin and cookie count.

findings.summary: The security policy is strong but incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, strict-origin referrer policy, frame-ancestors and Trusted Types; however Permissions-Policy is absent and style-src allows unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and migrate inline styles toward nonces/hashes where feasible while retaining Trusted Types and frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: Core public product content is effectively absent without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability captured 1% raw-to-rendered content coverage: raw HTML had 35 text characters and no title, H1 or meta description while the rendered page had 6,605 characters and 327 content tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the product title, description, primary actions and key sections, then hydrate enhancements rather than shipping a JS shell.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and omits responsive sizing.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found three oversized images, six without srcset and one legacy-format asset; the HAR includes a 424 KB PNG delivered at 2000x1283 for a 648 px display slot.
findings.suggestedFix: Use modern formats and responsive CDN parameters/srcset so each slot receives a near-display-size asset.

findings.summary: The page performs substantial work unrelated to the first user task.
findings.evidence: The 9.0 MB load includes 77 scripts, telemetry, feedback, Outlook app boot code and a video player; Lighthouse estimates 951 KiB of JS and 342 KiB CSS unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level resource budget and lazy-load feedback, video, app boot and analytics only when their feature becomes relevant.

findings.summary: Autoplay media and cross-origin assets dominate the resource budget.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found an autoplay video without controls or captions; HAR transferred 1.65 MB of media and 8.80 MB cross-origin on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not autoplay offscreen promotional media; use a poster and click-to-play control, captions where speech exists, and defer the player bundle.

findings.summary: The agent-oriented Outlook/Copilot surface exposes no structured browser capability on the public entry page.
findings.evidence: The site prominently links Copilot experiences, but DOM/source probes found no WebMCP or agent-tool registration and non-JS content coverage is only 1%.
findings.suggestedFix: For safe public actions such as sign-in help, plan lookup or product comparison, evaluate declarative agentic forms/WebMCP tools with strict schemas and user confirmation.

findings.summary: Heap growth after exercising tabs warrants a stabilized same-session leak investigation.
findings.evidence: Baseline summary was 49.5 MB/653,666 nodes; after dismissing consent and exercising tabs ten times it was 59.7 MB/839,165 nodes. The capture includes one-time full-page activation, so it is a risk signal rather than proof of a leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one stabilized session, force GC between phases, and investigate retained objects only if growth persists after tab cycles return to the same state.

findings.summary: The steady loaded footprint is large for a marketing entry page.
findings.evidence: The post-interaction heap summary reports 59.7 MB self size, 839,165 nodes and 3,056,272 edges, alongside a 9.0 MB transfer and duplicated app/marketing code.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate bundles and delay feature graphs so the marketing page creates only objects required for the visible route.
